editorial:
Imagine living through a massive earthquake that leaves your city in ruins and your government in a panic. That is where you start with this story. You get to follow Kiku and Tokachi, two strong women who fight in female sumo matches. While they are trying to make a living, they cross paths with a rebellious group called the Guillotine Society. These people want to change how the world works and aren't afraid to cause a scene. The movie feels like a mix of a sports drama and a political thriller, giving you a look at a side of history you probably never learned in school.

The acting is really strong, and you will feel for the characters as they struggle to survive. The pacing is a bit slow at times, but the emotional payoffs make it worth your while. If you like stories about underdogs fighting against the system, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heavy note as the government cracks down on the rebels. You see the members of the Guillotine Society get arrested and punished for their beliefs. Kiku and Tokachi realize that while they couldn't change the whole world, their bond and their strength gave them a sense of dignity. It wraps up by showing that the spirit of rebellion lives on even when the people are defeated.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and stories about fighting for justice.
